title: The open mapping lemma for complete linearly topologized groups
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a dichotomy for a continuous map of topologized abelian groups: if the target is separated and the source is complete, linearly topologized with a countable fundamental system of neighbourhoods of zero, then either the map is open or some open subgroup of the source has nowhere dense image (statement lines 9089-9099). The proof is a 21-line argument (proof lines 9102-9122): assuming the second alternative fails, the closures of the images of a nested fundamental system of subgroups are open and form a fundamental system in the target, one shows u(N_n) plus M_{n+1} equals M_n, chooses x_1 and then inductively elements y_i and x_{i+1} with u(y_i) + x_{i+1} = x_i, uses completeness of N to sum the y_i and separatedness of M to conclude that x_1 equals u(y), and then repeats the same argument to get M_i = u(N_i) for all i, which is openness. The two places where the topological hypotheses are really used are the formation of the sum of the y_i, which needs completeness, and the identification of the limit, which needs separatedness.
